_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); integrated oil and gas signals

pit_profile.why: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business involves exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas and manufacture, trade, transport and sale of crude oil, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemicals and a wide variety of specialty products'; 'The oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses are fundamentally commodity businesses. This means ExxonMobil’s operations and earnings may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas, and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among its risk factors, 'increased competitiveness of alternative energy sources' and 'Due to concern over the risks of climate change, a number of countries have adopted, or are considering the adoption of, regulatory frameworks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions', which 'could make our products more expensive, less competitive, lengthen project implementation times, and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shift hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon sources such as natural gas' (its own FY2018 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live (from 2015-12-12) and its climate-change risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for ExxonMobil

theme_watch.reason: Live: ExxonMobil's own FY2018 10-K, under 'Climate change and greenhouse gas restrictions', says 'Such policies could make our products more expensive, less competitive, lengthen project implementation times, and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shift hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon sources such as natural gas.' Under 'Government sponsorship of alternative energy': 'Our research projects focus on developing algae-based biofuels, carbon capture and storage, breakthrough energy efficiency processes, advanced energy-saving materials, and other technologies.' The stock trades at 15.9x FY19E — near its own median. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ENERGY_TRANSITION) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing decarbonisation of ExxonMobil's reserves and refining specifically.

classification.quality_note: ExxonMobil: 'Their principal business involves exploration for, and production of, crude oil and natural gas and manufacture, trade, transport and sale of crude oil, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemicals and a wide variety of specialty products'; 'The oil, gas, and petrochemical businesses are fundamentally commodity businesses. This means ExxonMobil’s operations and earnings may be significantly affected by changes in oil, gas, and petrochemical prices and by changes in margins on refined products'; 'The energy and petrochemical industries are highly competitive'; among its risk factors, 'increased competitiveness of alternative energy sources' and 'Due to concern over the risks of climate change, a number of countries have adopted, or are considering the adoption of, regulatory frameworks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions', which 'could make our products more expensive, less competitive, lengthen project implementation times, and reduce demand for hydrocarbons, as well as shift hydrocarbon demand toward relatively lower-carbon sources such as natural gas' (its own FY2018 10-K): earnings that move with the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live (from 2015-12-12) and its climate-change risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for ExxonMobil. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 5.01x; +22% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.46; conservative 2yr -10%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -51.2%/yr (worst year FY09-FY18, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-5.3%/yr (Q1 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +2.2%/yr (FY09-FY18 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +61.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY09-FY18); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: XOM (retrospective, 2019-06-21) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 5.01x (85.8% downside to Bear $11 / +17.1% upside to Bull $91) | Adj composite 2.20 vs market 2.66: gap -0.46 [MODESTLY OVERVALUED] | +22% above the EPP floor $63 (13x FY19E $4.88) | Conservative 2-yr case: -9.6% total (-4.8%/yr) | At 15.9x FY19E the 15% hurdle price $103 sits above the BULL case; oil-equivalent production +2.4% in Q1 2019, forward revenues -6.7% (no Q2 2019 revenue guide, Q1 2019 revenue as reported); the energy transition is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
